**Goal `coalesce-assign` — `??=` works as PHP's does, and `??+=`, `??-=` and `??.=` start from a default — has its decision record and nothing of its behaviour yet.** Goal `program-enumeration`'s whole list is this goal's Stage 1 floor.

ADR 0254 is on disk and is the goal's one record: it `creates` `rule:expressions/defaulting-assignment`
(status `designed`, empty `guardedBy`, flipped to `shipped` with its two Stage 3 cases) and `modifies`
`rule:php-migration/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value`, whose `because` already names 0254. That
fragment's **prose is unchanged on purpose**: it is still true until `??=` writes an absent key, so its
second paragraph is rewritten in the commit that lands item 2 below, not before. ADR 0254 § 7 and § 8
are the decision a Stage 2 session implements; the goal file's § *Standing decisions* is the source.

The tree as it stands: `check_compound_assign` returns the target's type for every operator, so
`return $this->x ??= f();` is `E0403` against a non-null return type. `$options["theme"] ??= "light"`
on an absent key throws `undefined array key`, which is gap `nvs-ir/throws-on-an-array-key-that`, and
that gap's record says why marking `Env::coalesce_guarded` alone turns an `E0482` into a panic.
`$a ??+= 1` is a parse error (`E0102`).

items.text: **The guarded read of a compound target** (ADR 0254 § 7) — `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/assign.rs:1290` (`check_compound_assign`) marks the target's levels for the read when the operator is `??=`, with the walk `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/presence.rs:100` (`mark_guarded_places`) is; the mark is one the read consults and the write does not, so `crates/nvs-ir/src/lower/stmt.rs:1554` (`row_ty_of`) still sees the ordinary row and `array<?array<int>> $g; $g["0"]["1"] ??= 5;` stays `E0482`. Take it together with the next item: neither is testable alone.

**An absent key is written** (ADR 0254 § 7) — `crates/nvs-ir/src/lower/stmt.rs:538` (`lower_compound_assignment`) goes through `lower_read_modify_write`: the read of the target is the guarded one at every level, and the write is the plain one, so `$g["k"]["j"] ??= 5` with no `"k"` creates the row. In the same commit: gap `data/gaps/nvs-ir/throws-on-an-array-key-that.json` is deleted, example 03 of `and-the-ternary` loses its `// proof: gap` line, and the second paragraph of `docs/rules/php-migration/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value.md` is rewritten whole to say the target of `??=` is the same guarded read, then `bun nv rules --render`.

**The result type** (ADR 0254 § 8) — `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/assign.rs:1329` (`check_compound_assign`'s return) returns, for `??=` alone, the target's type with `null` removed when the value's type has no `null`; every other operator and `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/assign.rs:728` (`check_assign`)'s plain `=` keep the target's type. Check the IR value's representation in a value position (`$x = ($o->p ??= v)`) agrees with the narrowed type; the pack's trap `?T ?? <literal>` is `mixed` is near this.

**The two conformance cases and the named tests** of the goal file's Stage 2 checks, the hooked-property test in `crates/nvs-ir/src/lower/tests.rs:67` (beside `lower_script_src`) included; each new case is added to the `guardedBy` of `data/rules/php-migration/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value.json`.
